ambiguities.text: Behavior for first byte value 0xff (reserved) is not specified
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume transactions starting with 0xff are rejected as invalid until a future EIP defines their meaning.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'SHOULD include the TransactionType as the first byte of the signed data' is a recommendation, not requirement
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume compliant implementations MUST include the type byte in signed data to prevent cross-type signature reuse attacks, treating this as a de facto requirement.

ambiguities.text: The boundary between typed [0x00-0x7f] and legacy [0xc0-0xfe] transactions leaves gap [0x80-0xbf] undefined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume bytes in range [0x80-0xbf] are invalid and transactions should be rejected. This range would be valid RLP list starts that are too short to be valid legacy transactions.

implicit_assumptions.description: New transaction types will be introduced only through the EIP process with proper security review
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious or poorly designed transaction types could introduce consensus vulnerabilities or security holes

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot create a valid signature for a different transaction type using the same signed data
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Signature replay attacks across transaction types, allowing transactions to be executed with unintended semantics

implicit_assumptions.description: All nodes on the network support the same set of activated transaction types at any given block height
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Network partition or consensus failures if nodes disagree on valid transaction types for a block

implicit_assumptions.description: Wallet software will correctly implement type-specific signing to include the type byte
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users could sign transactions that are vulnerable to type-confusion attacks if wallets omit type byte from signed data
